pairs.subject: structured-output
pairs.evidence: src/lib/athena/actions-execute.ts:169 The ruling executor forwards a nonempty model-supplied finding key to the decision upsert without resolving the finding, allowing nonexistent targets to become durable decisions.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/athena/[id]/message/route.ts:75 Each interactive request starts a turn without server-side per-thread admission; the client sending flag cannot prevent concurrent callers from running against the same thread.
src/lib/athena/actions.ts:353 The action producer requests fenced text rather than assembling independently contributed decoder constraints.
src/lib/llm/tool-loop.ts:195 The assembled Athena leg carries tools and no output constraint, so the conflicting combination does not arise.
src/lib/athena/blocks.ts:294 Although extraction removes payload spans, block-only output receives synthesized narration, "Here it is.", contrary to the explicit empty-narration rule.
src/lib/athena/actions.ts:546 Aggregate drops discard the distinction between malformed JSON, unknown actions and parameter failures, along with rejected candidates needed for diagnosis.
src/lib/athena/actions.ts:520 Action fence bodies receive strict parsing followed by dropping on failure, without a tolerant recovery ladder or a recorded strategy trace.
src/lib/athena/turn.ts:304 This persisted episode is a derived exchange summary, not an artifact claiming verbatim source spans.

src/lib/athena/actions-execute.ts:169 The catalog closes operation names, but rule_on_finding does not resolve its operative itemKey before recording a ruling; decide performs a tenant-scoped upsert rather than a finding lookup.
src/lib/athena/actions.ts:384 Numeric action parameters are silently converted to strings, and successful validation carries no coercion or repair record.

pairs.subject: structured-output
pairs.evidence: src/lib/llm/provider.ts:236 The validator silently rounds and clamps model scores into legal values instead of rejecting invalid values or producing an explicit repair outcome.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/llm/provider.ts:390 The named coverage floor and deduplication exist, but this count includes scores rounded or clamped by validateAssessment; five scores of 250 become five scores of 100 and satisfy a nine-dimension request's floor.
src/lib/llm/gemini.ts:91 This assessment request has one built-in schema rather than multiple independently contributed constraints competing for capacity.
src/lib/llm/openai.ts:93 The inspected assessment request supplies an output format without acting tools; Bedrock instead uses a reporting tool's input schema.
src/lib/llm/provider.ts:365 This seam returns a machine assessment rather than a conversational turn with separate narration; presentation occurs downstream.

src/lib/llm/schema.ts:176 The OpenAI schema transformation removes numeric bounds without replacing the small integer score domain with a derived enumeration, leaving range enforcement to post-generation clamping.
src/lib/llm/json.ts:21 Parse failure retains only a short head snippet, without the required tail, strategy trace or final validation errors; successful parsing also exposes no strategy telemetry.

src/lib/llm/json.ts:119 The generic syntax extractor ranks candidates using assessment-specific dimensions fields, mixing validation concerns into extraction and returning no winning-strategy or multi-candidate metadata.
src/lib/llm/bedrock.ts:212 The reporting tool's input is consumed as assessment data rather than dispatched as a model-proposed operation.

src/lib/llm/output-budget.ts:79 Measurement and warning bands exist, but the default gemini-3.8-flash matches none of the listed Gemini prefixes and receives the wholly-unknown fallback instead of a recognized-family default.

src/lib/llm/provider.ts:236 Fractional and out-of-range scores silently become valid integers; the validator returns an assessment instead of path-addressed rejection errors and a bounded semantic repair outcome.

pairs.registryProposal: Clarify multi-candidate ownership: the fenced-block rung says to prefer the candidate that validates furthest, while the cross-rung rule forbids schema consultation; specify how validator-ranked selection should occur without assessment-specific heuristics inside a generic extractor.
